cards.claim: Performance improves predictably with training time, dataset size, and model size across many orders of magnitude
cards.conditions: Neural networks on a variety of tasks, trained with gradient descent
cards.effect: Consistent improvement in performance across three independent scaling axes
cards.evidence: Empirical observation across multiple domains (general scaling law phenomenon)
cards.quote: On a variety of tasks, the performance of neural networks predictably improves with training time, dataset size and model size across many orders of magnitude.

cards.claim: Scaling of performance with training time and model size follow different power law exponents
cards.conditions: Random feature model trained with gradient descent; applicable to network training generally
cards.effect: Asymmetric scaling relationships: time and model size contribute unequally to performance gains
cards.evidence: Theoretical prediction from solvable random feature model
cards.quote: First, our model makes a prediction about why the scaling of performance with training time and with model size have different power law exponents.

cards.claim: Asymmetric compute-optimal scaling rule: training steps should be increased faster than model parameters
cards.conditions: Compute-optimal regime; assumes fixed computational budget
cards.effect: At fixed compute, greater improvements from increasing steps than from increasing model width
cards.evidence: Theory consistent with recent empirical observations
cards.quote: Consequently, the theory predicts an asymmetric compute-optimal scaling rule where the number of training steps are increased faster than model parameters, consistent with recent empirical observations.

cards.claim: Convergence rate to infinite-width dynamics transitions from width-independent (1/width) early in training to width-dependent (width^-c) late in training
cards.conditions: Neural network training; transition occurs between early and late training phases; c depends on architecture and task structure
cards.effect: Width effects on learning dynamics change in magnitude and form over training
cards.evidence: Theoretical model exhibiting this behavior; observations from prior work
cards.quote: Second, it has been observed that early in training, networks converge to their infinite-width dynamics at a rate $1/\textit{width}$ but at late time exhibit a rate $\textit{width}^{-c}$, where $c$ depends on the structure of the architecture and task.

cards.claim: Training-test loss gap grows over time due to repeated reuse of the same data
cards.conditions: Finite dataset, multiple training epochs causing data reuse
cards.effect: Generalization gap accumulates with training duration independent of model capacity
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis showing how data reuse affects the gap
cards.quote: Lastly, our theory shows how the gap between training and test loss can gradually build up over time due to repeated reuse of data.
